title: An infant cohort model ranks perinatal features for gastrointestinal outcomes
summary: A random-forest analysis of 6,060 infants ranked birth weight, cord-blood pH and maternal age as important features for recorded first-year gastrointestinal-disorder labels. The result describes model importance in one hospital cohort, not causal risk factors or a validated preventive-care tool.
organization: University of Salento; University of Naples Federico II

source_review.scope: Official primary BioC original article sections: Participants/outcome reference;ML/preprocessing/feature selection;random-forest ranking Results and model limitations; no laboratory-method validation

evidence.ai_role: A fitted random forest ranks variables by impurity reduction when classifying clinician-assessed colic, regurgitation and constipation outcomes. The learned ranking, not conventional regression alone, enables the represented feature pattern.
evidence.tested: Outcomes were assessed by a trained pediatrician using RomeIV criteria during first-year follow-up. The source reports a 70:30 split, model comparisons and weighted-average F1 of0.74, without a complete condition-specific independent-validation account.
evidence.unknown: Prospective enrollment is distinct from model locking before new outcomes. Preprocessing/feature-selection containment and class resampling details are incomplete. Impurity importance can favor continuous variables and does not establish effect direction or causation. The source alternates between the random-forest classification model and a logistic-regression web tool; no deployed-tool accuracy, prevention benefit or independent cohort confirmation is represented.
